title: Private VPC control plane playbook — regulatory pitch & objection handling
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working playbook for GTM folks (AEs, Solutions Eng, Product Marketing) and PMs to align on messaging for our Private deployment offering (VPC / on-prem control plane) targeted at regulated customers. Focus: control-plane language, data residency, and concise rebuttals to common buyer objections.

Quick elevator (30s):
For teams that can’t send sensitive data to shared, multi-tenant clouds, Redwood Private provides the same developer API and runtime as our hosted service but with a customer-managed control plane that runs in your VPC (or air-gapped data center). That means equivalent latency/throughput guarantees, full key custody, and audit-grade telemetry — while preserving operator-level controls your security, compliance, and procurement teams require.

Primary audiences & typical buyer stakeholders:
- Platform/Infra Engineering (primary technical evaluator): cares about networking, deployment automation, and observability integration.
- Security / InfoSec: checks data flow, egress, KMS/HSM, vulnerability surface, pen test history.
- Legal / Compliance / Privacy: requires audit trails, data residency, contracts (DPA, SCCs), SOC/ISO certifications.
- ML/Product engineering: concerned about model parity, latency, and developer ergonomics (same API/SDK, feature parity).
- Procurement / Finance: TCO, licensing model, support SLAs, contract length.

Core positioning pillars (short bullets for customer-facing collateral):
1) Customer-first control plane: customer-managed control plane that can be deployed in a VPC or on-prem; Redwood’s control plane artifacts are deployed as customer-owned infra resources or run in an isolated management VPC under your account.
2) Zero-surprise telemetry: outbound telemetry is opt-in; when enabled it uses customer-provided endpoints/forwarders; can integrate with SIEM/Syslog or on-prem ELK.
3) Key custody & encryption: native KMS and HSM integrations (bring-your-own) — model weights and token caches can be encrypted at rest with customer keys.
4) Compliance-ready defaults: audit logs, immutable request traces, retention controls, and compliance packaging to speed SOC/ISO readiness.
5) Operational parity: same API surface as hosted (streaming, function calls, rollouts) and Redwood-provided runbooks for autoscaling and capacity planning.
6) Predictable economics: reserved capacity and committed pricing options for dedicated Private clusters to avoid surprise egress/usage bills.

Message framing by persona:
- For Security: emphasize minimal trust surface (no forced outbound), BYOK and HSM support, signed telemetry, and comprehensive audit log. Offer a short network diagram showing control-plane endpoints inside the customer VPC and optional air-gap architecture.
- For Platform: stress IaC templates (Terraform), CI/CD examples, and compatibility with existing cluster autoscalers. Show how we support private image registries and restricted egress.
- For ML/Product: highlight that model variants and rollouts are identical to hosted: same SDKs, same caching & batching improvements, and Redwood Optimize recommendations apply.
- For Legal/Compliance: provide DPA & standard contract addenda, SOC2/ISO checklist, and references for data residency.
- For Procurement: present a 3-tier purchasing path: PoC (time-boxed usage), Reserved cluster (commit pricing), Enterprise private license (term + premium SLAs).

Top buyer objections and suggested rebuttals (script snippets):
1) Objection: "We can’t allow any external control plane — it’s a hard no."
   Rebuttal: "Understood. We offer a customer-managed control plane model where all control-plane components are deployed into your account/VPC. Outbound connections are unnecessary; we support completely isolated deployments with admin access delivered via your VPN/Jumpbox."
   Evidence: architecture diagram + brief on air-gapped deployment checklist.

2) Objection: "How do we trust you with telemetry/telemetry backdoors?"
   Rebuttal: "Telemetry is opt-in. When enabled it forwards to your endpoints and is signed. We also publish a minimal telemetry spec and provide an audit of what fields are emitted. For high-assurance customers we can disable telemetry and rely on your log collection."

3) Objection: "Key management and encryption — who holds keys?"
   Rebuttal: "You do. We support AWS KMS/RSA HSM integrations and a BYOK flow. Keys never leave your KMS; Redwood only holds ephemeral references to encrypted artifacts. We can append HSM attestation docs for legal review."

4) Objection: "Is performance the same as hosted?"
   Rebuttal: "Same runtime and kernels; performance parity depends on your infra. We provide validated instance types and deployment recipes used by customers achieving <50ms p50 token latencies. Our SRE team will run a perf validation as part of the PoC."

5) Objection: "This sounds expensive to operate and lock us in."
   Rebuttal: "We provide cost models, reserved capacity options, and migration playbooks. The control plane is ephemeral — models and runtime artifacts are exportable; customers can move workloads back to hosted or another cluster with the same SDK."

Competitive notes (concise):
- General cloud AI platforms (big cloud vendors): Strength = deep cloud integrations and managed infra; Weakness = multi-tenant telemetry/limited BYOK options and slower feature parity for inference-specific performance tweaks.
- Managed LLM APIs (hosted-first vendors): Strength = easy to ship; Weakness = poor fit for regulated data and limited private options.
- Self-hosted runtimes / OSS + integrators: Strength = full control; Weakness = heavy ops burden and no single-vendor SLA for performance + orchestration.
Where Redwood wins: unified developer experience across all modes (hosted/dedicated/private), production-first runtime optimizations, and enterprise controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs, rollouts) bundled with a support SLA and migration tooling.

POC / Demo checklist for SEs (pre-sales):
- Collect: network diagram, allowed egress list, preferred KMS/HSM, certificate authority, and compliance gatekeepers (SOC/PCI/etc.).
- Offer: Terraform module + CloudFormation sample for control-plane bootstrap, a sample policy for security team review, and a small perf test harness that runs on-prem or in-customer VPC.
- Success criteria: ability to call the API from a dev environment with latency < target, audit log capture confirmed in customer SIEM, and key import verification.

Suggested collateral and artifacts to produce (short-term):
- One-pager: "How Redwood Private control plane works — for InfoSec" (diagram + 6 bullets)
- Network diagram pack: isolated, transit-gateway, and air-gapped variants
- POC runbook: checklist + timelines + success metrics (for SEs to hand to customers)
- Compliance appendix: mapping to SOC2/ISO/PCI expectations and sample contract clauses

Proof points & datasheet bullets to collect from Eng/SRE:
- Typical p50/p95 token latency for our recommended instance types (hosted vs private)
- Throughput (tokens/s) per GPU family with our runtime + quantization notes
- Example: Customer X (anonymous) achieved 60% token-cost reduction vs baseline via caching/batching on Private cluster.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):

- [TODO] Validate air-gapped deployment checklist with SRE (owner: Lina) — due 2025-02-11.

- [QUESTION] Which contract addendum templates are legally necessary vs recommended for APAC customers? (owner: Legal)

Notes / negotiation tips for AEs:
- Offer a time-boxed, low-fee PoC to reduce procurement friction.
- Pre-fill the security questionnaire where possible — customers hate repetitive forms.
- Where customers ask for SLA language, start with commitment to response/SE support and a follow-up premium SLA offering after validated run.

Slack links & references for quick access:
- SE PoC repo: git.internal.redwood/private-poc (ask SE lead for access)
- Slack channel: #private-deploys for live support during demos
- Confluence: PRIVATE-CONTROL-PLANE-OVERVIEW (detailed infra diagrams and runbooks)

Appendix: short sample objection play (for SDR/AE practice):
"Security lead: 'We don't allow any telemetry off-network.'
AE: 'Totally understandable — we built Private to support that exact requirement. We can disable telemetry by default and run a closed PoC that sends logs only to your SIEM. Our control plane can be fully deployed inside your VPC and administered via your VPN. Would it help if I set up a 30-min architecture review with our SRE and your security team?'"

End of draft — feedback welcome.
Unresolved: need legal/infra signoff on the exact wording for "control-plane under your account" — some customers will parse this for ownership and liability.

---
Notes-to-self: keep language plain, avoid 'black box' implications, and always lead with customer control, then follow with performance and economics.
